title: Policy bundle manifest (ACP-SPEC-001 §8.2)
description: Identity and provenance of one signed policy bundle. PB-5: bundle_epoch is strictly increasing and never reused or decreased. PB-2: author and reviewer identities MUST differ — asserted by the signer, because a schema cannot express a comparison between two of its own fields.

schema_version.description: Version of this manifest schema. Present so a decoder can refuse a bundle it does not fully understand rather than ignoring fields it does not recognise.

bundle_epoch.description: PB-5. Strictly increasing integer. Never reused, never decreased. The Executor keeps a high-water mark indefinitely (CL-4) — an expiring epoch mark would reopen rollback.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC. Informational: freshness is enforced by expires_at and by the epoch, never by comparing this to a local clock.

author.description: Who wrote this bundle. PB-2: MUST differ from reviewer.

reviewer.description: Who reviewed it. PB-2: MUST differ from author. Two-person integrity on the highest-leverage governance artifact in the system — RES-1 names floor maintenance as exactly that.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC. PB-1: the engine MUST refuse to serve an expired bundle. A deployment MAY configure a grace window during which all Decisions are capped at ATTEST — it may not configure one that serves the bundle normally.

min_suite.description: CR-4. The signed floor on signature suites. A receipt or attestation declaring a weaker suite is refused. This is in the signed bundle precisely so a downgrade cannot be negotiated at runtime.

id.description: Stable identifier. Compared byte-for-byte for PB-2; display_name is never used for the comparison because two people can share a display name.

custody.description:
How the bundle signing key is held.

CLASSIFIED **T** (trusted as transmitted) AND NOT A CONTROL INPUT. A verifier MUST NOT weight any decision on this object. A bundle asserting its own custody strength is the recurring defect RES-8/RES-9/RES-10 names: a verifier must never accept a derived security value from the party it is verifying. A compromised signer writes this object freely.

It is recorded for humans — auditors, operators, and the reviewer named above — and for no other purpose. The real binding is that the verifier is configured out of band with the expected public key.

tier.description: T0 development only; T1 encrypted key on an air-gapped host; T2 non-exportable cloud KMS; T3 PKCS#11 HSM. Split custody reports the WEAKER of its two legs, because a claim should never round in the flattering direction.

custody_leg.description: Custody of one primitive. The two legs may differ, and differing is not a weakness: verification is conjunctive (CR-3), so forging requires BOTH signatures and therefore BOTH keys. An attacker must defeat both mechanisms.

mechanism.description: Free text naming the concrete mechanism, e.g. "YubiHSM2 slot 3" or "age-encrypted file, offline laptop". Human-readable only.
